problems.text: The new assertions still fail with the warm-up working once the machine is loaded well beyond the level the brief set. They meet the brief's bar: with four runs at once nothing failed (9 of 9 real test runs, 0 of 27 measured pairs), and with eight at once 0 of 48 pairs. With sixteen copies of the real test at once, 4 of 16 failed on JDK 21 and 4 of 16 on JDK 25, and 10 of 16 needed their second pair on each. All eight failures were the 0.75 early-rise relation summed over two pairs; the 0.85 relation never failed a two-pair sum. In 32 measured pairs at that load, 18 failed singly (17 on the 0.75 relation, 1 on the 0.85 one). The cause is the one the open item named, the 3-second cap of the warm-up: 30 rounds take about 0.6 s alone, and a harness run took 18 to 27 s at this load against 5 to 7 s with four at once. With the rounds cut by hand (DLA_WARM_ROUNDS on the warm side, four at once, JDK 21) the 0.75 ratio was 0.51 to 0.63 at 15 rounds, 0.57 to 0.79 at 8 and 0.76 to 0.89 at 3. The second pair does not help while the load lasts. On JDK 25 the HEAD assertions failed 0 of 16 pairs at this load, because the 500 KB line kept the comparison off there. The row gives the 0.75 ratio as 0.29 to 0.64 and does not say at what load the relation stops holding. Direction: state the limit in the row, or drop or loosen the 0.75 relation.

The row says the unit test was seen failing 'with the skip off: total 5 where 2 is expected'. The test now feeds four recorder threads, so the skip off gives 6. I ran it on a scratch copy of the crate: total 6. The other figure in the row is right: with only `JFR Recording Scheduler` left out the total is 3.

This row still describes the warm-up test as asserting 'rise over 14 checkpoints with the warm-up under 0.75 of the rise without'. After this pass the test asserts the rise from the first reading under 0.85 of the cold run's, and the 0.75 comparison only on Linux with a cold rise of 250 KB or more. The sentence was already inexact at HEAD and was not updated when the test changed.

Wording. The comment and the row say the 0.85 line 'lies between the ranges' straight after quoting 0.72 to 1.38 for two cold runs; 0.85 is inside that range. It lies between the ranges measured in this pass only (at most 0.54 against at least 0.88; mine were 0.53 and 0.90 with four at once). The row's last sentence does admit the 0.72. The comment also says the early-rise relation applies where the cold rise is 'about 0.3 MB or more', and the code uses 250 KB.

The row now names the six `attach_tools` tests that failed on the runner and gives no local count, saying the number depends on the stand-in. The tests that failed only here stay unnamed. The claim is true as written; the open item's wish to name them is met only by dropping the count.

The location check does not try the mixed spellings that `isTestLocation` now tries. A project given by a link, with a class location that goes through a link inside the project to a directory outside it, is not counted as the project's. The old and the new agent behave the same (both false in my hand run), so this is not a regression and not part of the open item.

Plan names remain in M7 rows that the open items did not name: 'round 1', 'round-1', 'round 2', 'P3', 'P4', 'E3', 'U3'. The fixer's report lists only 438, 450, 451 and 469. Row 450 still points at 'the P4 row', the same kind of pointer as 'the last U4 row'. The row that the new pointer in row 447 names still has 'B0' in its own title, outside the M7 table. None of the twelve rows changed in this pass holds a plan name.

The early-rise relation is switched off by operating system. The macOS logs give 0.94 and 1.09 for it, with a cold rise of 336 to 347 KB that is above the 250 KB line, so only the Linux condition keeps it off there. Every Linux measurement is x86-64 and the macOS runner is arm64, so whether the difference comes from the OS or the CPU is not known. It matters only if the tests ever run on Linux arm64.
